The waggle dance explained

Forager honeybees returning to the hive perform a waggle dance on the vertical comb. The angle of the waggle run relative to straight up matches the angle between the food source and the sun. A run straight up means fly toward the sun; a run straight down means fly away from it.

The duration of the waggle run encodes distance: roughly one second of waggling corresponds to about one kilometre of flight. Bees watching the dance follow the dancer and then fly out in that direction and for that distance.

Dances for richer food sources are repeated more often, so more bees are recruited to the best patches. This lets a colony spread its foragers efficiently across many flowers.
